title: Adaptive trigger orchestrator for region/tier routing & circuit harmonization
creator: Ava Patel
description: Goal: implement a unified 'Adaptive Trigger Orchestrator' that harmonizes automatic fallback triggers across region selection, tier routing, and model-variant circuit-breakers. The orchestrator will synthesize signals (429 spikes, request timeouts, 5xx error rates, token-level latency percentiles) into tenant- and route-scoped decisions to: 1) initiate soft fallbacks to lower-cost/compatible model variants, 2) perform regional cutovers, and 3) open/close circuit breakers with decay/probation windows. This ticket codifies thresholds, signal fusion strategy, telemetry requirements, and a safe rollout plan for production traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator computes a composite failure score per route and tenant using configured signal weights
When composite score crosses configured thresholds, orchestrator triggers the appropriate action (soft fallback, regional failover, or circuit open) within 5s of signal arrival
Circuit open/close actions honor tenant-specific SLA tiers and cooldown decay profiles
All actions are traceable in Console (audit event, route-level annotation, and rollout timeline) and have associated metrics for success/failure
Automated e2e chaos test demonstrates graceful fallback during synthetic 429/timeouts with no more than 2x token-latency increase for affected traffic
implementation_plan: 1) Define composite scoring model: signals = {429_rate, timeout_rate, 5xx_rate, p95_token_latency, queue_depth}, configurable weights per project/tier
2) Implement signal ingestion pipeline (aggregated 1s windows) in routing control plane; reuse existing streaming telemetry collector
3) Build score evaluator microservice with REST/GRPC interface that returns action: NO_OP | SOFT_FALLBACK(model_variant) | REGION_FAILOVER(region_id) | OPEN_CIRCUIT(duration_ms)
4) Extend router to call evaluator synchronously for high-risk requests and cache decisions for short TTL to avoid thundering (configurable cache 250-2000ms)
5) Add circuit state machine: CLOSED -> PROBATION -> OPEN -> HALF_OPEN -> CLOSED with exponential backoff and configurable decay rates per tenant tier
6) Wire Console audit events and dashboards: expose composite score, action history, and per-tenant thresholds
7) Add unit tests, integration tests (local and staging), and a chaos test harness that simulates 429 spikes and regional network partitions
8) Prepare migration: default safe weights, opt-in feature flag per org, and rollback path (global kill-switch)
9) Run canary on internal tenant beta1 (5% traffic) then expand to 25% with automated rollback on regression signals
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature gated behind org-level opt-in; telemetry-only mode for 2 weeks to collect baseline scores
Phase 1: Canary to 5% of traffic for non-critical tiers (dev/test orgs); monitor composite score and false-positive fallback rate
Phase 2: Ramp to 25% with tenant-tier-aware rollout (exclude enterprise SLA customers unless explicitly opted-in)
Phase 3: Full rollout with default conservative thresholds and telemetry-derived tuning recommendations
Rollback: Immediate feature toggle to telemetry-only and manual revert of cache entries; automated rollback if token-drop or error-rate increases > 10% for > 3 minutes
telemetry_queries: PromQL: sum(rate(request_timeouts[1m])) by (route,tenant) / sum(rate(http_requests[1m])) by (route,tenant) -> timeout_rate

BigQuery: SELECT route, tenant, APPROX_QUANTILES(token_lat_ms, 100)[OFFSET(95)] as p95 FROM token_latency WHERE _PARTITIONTIME > TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 HOUR) GROUP BY route, tenant
Dashboard panels: composite_score (1s rollup), action_rate (actions/sec), circuit_state_counts by tenant and region
risk_and_tradeoffs: Pros: centralized decisioning avoids inconsistent per-router heuristics and simplifies operator reasoning; enables tenant-specific tuning
Cons: introduces a centralized dependency in the routing path that must be highly available and low-latency; mitigated by caching and local fallback policies
Tradeoff: synchronous evaluator calls reduce time to mitigation but increase request path latency — we mitigate with short TTL caching and async probes
False positives: conservative default thresholds and probation windows to reduce unnecessary fallbacks that could affect quality
security_considerations: Evaluator service must authenticate router calls with mTLS
Audit events include minimal PII; only tenant and route identifiers
No model weights or customer data will traverse evaluator — decisions are based on aggregated telemetry
open_questions: Should confidence of decision be surfaced to Console? (proposed: yes, as a 0-100 composite score)
Default weight values per signal for each tenant tier — propose conservative starting weights (429:0.4, timeout:0.3, 5xx:0.2, p95_latency:0.1)
How to handle cascading region failovers when inter-region latency spikes cause mirrored errors? Consider global dampening window
What SLA tiers are allowed automatic regional cutover by default? (suggest: only P2/P3 by default; P0/P1 require explicit opt-in)
